name: Patent Filings
blurb:
This section tracks cumulative AI-related patent counts for 108 companies, ranking them by total portfolio size and charting how the combined total moves over time. It answers who is building the largest patent positions in AI, not who is inventing the most cutting-edge techniques right now, since raw filing counts favor large, long-established portfolios over newer, more selective filers.

The total is checked daily but only changes in step jumps every five to seven days, so it is best read as a periodically refreshed patent-database snapshot rather than a live daily count of new filings. Filing databases also lag actual invention by months given publication delays, and patent volume says nothing about which filings cover techniques that matter commercially or turn out to be defensible.

As of September 5, 2026, the tracked total stands at 312,470 AI-related patents across the 108 companies, up from 310,516 three weeks earlier, a gain of about 1,954 patents, or roughly 650 per week. Samsung leads by a wide margin with 108,943 patents, more than the next three companies combined, IBM at 69,827, Apple at 31,794, and Huawei at 27,442. Microsoft follows at 24,682. Further down, chip and model companies file far less by volume. NVIDIA holds 3,489, Meta 2,684, and Palantir 1,668, reflecting narrower but more targeted AI patent strategies. The count also tracks granted patents rather than pending applications, so it understates real activity for companies whose recent filings are still in prosecution and have not yet issued.

reading.body:
Patent counts measure the size and age of a company's legal portfolio, not its current AI capability. Samsung holds 109,889 patents, more than the next three companies combined, while NVIDIA holds 3,489 and Meta 2,684.

The tracked total across 108 companies runs from 310,516 on August 14, 2026 to 472,484 on October 3, 2026. That is not steady growth. The series is flat for days at a time, then jumps: 312,470 to 453,494 between September 10 and September 13, and 458,754 to 471,785 between September 30 and October 1. These are database refresh events, not bursts of invention. The blurb states the total is checked daily but changes in step jumps every five to seven days, and that publication lag puts filings months behind the work they describe.

For AI specifically, the ranking is close to useless as a map of who is building. The largest positions belong to hardware and legacy software firms, Samsung, IBM, TSMC, Intel, Micron, whose portfolios accumulated over decades and span far more than AI. The companies whose AI systems define the field file far less by volume. A patent count cannot distinguish a defensible claim from a defensive one, and granted patents exclude pending applications, which understates recent filers.

What the data does not cover: which filings concern AI at all, what they claim, whether they are licensed or litigated, or how any of it connects to compute, buildings, or power. Nothing here speaks to data centers, electricity, or chips. It is a count of legal instruments, refreshed in batches, and should be read as one.
